 A Message After Midterms
 Nov 5 
 Written by Isabelle Redfield 
 By The Conservateur 
 Official U.S. Department of Interior Photo by Andrew King 
 “Be not overcome of evil, but overcome evil with good.” — Romans 12:21
 The election results on Tuesday were brutal. No doubt about it. But we’re not dissuaded. The Conservateur is more fired up than ever about the prospect of creating a new generational movement of America First, conservative, Christian values.
 If you look at many of the ballot measures passed across swing states, it’s clear Republicans lost this election. Leftism did not win. Wokeism and socialism are still deeply unpopular. The progressive movement is fundamentally out of touch with families across America, and just like in 2020, people will soon be turned off by their insane ideological culture wars, anti-Americanism, hostility toward faith and family, and incompetency. Over the next two years, DSA candidates will almost certainly alienate normal people who simply want a safe, affordable place to raise their children.
 Democrats have built a coalition around grievance, anger, identity politics, abortion fanaticism, genderqueer ideology, unassimilated immigration, government dependency, and an activist class that looks down on the values millions of Americans hold dear.
 The Republican Party must strive to be the party of everyday, normal, working-class Americans. We must build a policy platform that prioritizes family formation and making the American dream achievable.
 Conservative Christian Gen Z men need to step up and run for Congress in 2028. We need a new generation of leaders to inspire an America First, pro-family movement of American patriots.
 We want our children to inherit a country where faith is sacred, hard work is respected, and family is the bedrock of our nation. That is the America First movement The Conservateur wants to help build.
 Join us as we look ahead to 2028 with resolute faith in God’s plan for America. As Charlie Kirk said: “Be joyful warriors.”
 Isabelle Redfield
